report.summary: The one failing test, test_book_can_be_updated, is a test bug: it sends year=2001 in the PUT but asserts the stored year is 2002. The app stores the submitted value unchanged and the response is correct, so the fix is to correct the expected year in tests/api/test_books_api.py:27 to 2001 (or send 2002 if that was the intent). No product or infrastructure fault is involved.

causes.title: test_book_can_be_updated asserts year 2002 after updating to year 2001
causes.explanation: The test PUTs year=2001 (line 23) and then expects the fetched book to have year=2002 (line 27). The application's update path writes book.year unchanged, so the stored value is 2001, which is what the app returned. The expected literal is a typo or stale value. The app's year handling has no code path that adds one to a year. The seeded year_off_by_one bug only relaxes the upper bound in validate_book (app/main.py:94), so it does not change stored values.
evidence: tests/api/test_books_api.py:23: updated = api.update_book(book["id"], title="Final title", author="Someone", year=2001)
app/main.py:232-235: UPDATE books SET title = ?, author = ?, year = ? ... return {"id": book_id, **book.model_dump()}; no year transformation
The only occurrences of 2001 or 2002 in the repo are on lines 23 and 27 of the test file.
causes.suggested_fix: In tests/api/test_books_api.py line 27, change "year": 2002 to "year": 2001 so it matches the value sent on line 23. Alternatively, change line 23 to year=2002 if that was the intended value, and keep both lines consistent.
